subject: 'could not find function "read.table"' when using load_all

messages.author: 62f1f02184823e09
messages.subject: 'could not find function "read.table"' when using load_all
parts:
Hi

I am developing a package which contains data. When I use load_all("./") I get the error below, but load_data("./") works. The error message is:

  Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) (from SPECIESECON.R#27) : could not find function "read.table"

The "offending" file (./data/SPECIESECON.R) looks as follow:

SPECIESECON <- local({
     con <- textConnection(
       "\"fullName\" \"espre\" \"IFNName\" \"color\"
\"1\" \"Quercus robur\" \"1\" \"quercus_robur\" \"green\"
\"2\" \"Quercus peatrea\" \"2\" \"quercus_peatrea\" \"blue\"
\"3\" \"Fagus sylvatica\" \"4\" \"fagus_sylvatica\" \"red\"
\"4\" \"Picae abies\" \"7\" \"picae_abies\" \"pink\"
\"5\" \"Abies alba\" \"8\" \"abies_alba\" \"brown\""
     )
     res <- read.table(
       con,
       header    = TRUE,
       row.names = 1,
       sep       = "\t",
       as.is     = TRUE
     )
     close(con)
     res
   })

I assume that it has to do with the local() but I want to use the file as it is as it i=s generate=d from orgmode (emacs).

messages.author: 62f1f02184823e09
messages.subject: SOLVED: 'could not find function "read.table"' when using load_all
parts:
SOLVED: I just checked it without the local, and I get the same error.

The problem was that I have to use utils::read.table instead of read.table.

Cheers,

Rainer

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: 'could not find function "read.table"' when using load_all
parts:
I don't recommend using .R files in the data directory, but the likely
problem is that the utils package is not on the search path. Just do
utils::read.table().

Hadley

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: 'could not find function "read.table"' when using load_all
parts:
> I guess your recommendation is based on incompatibilities between versions
> of R?

A few reasons:

* How data/*.R is really poorly documented

* This code is run every time you reload the package

* I think it's better to have the data in version control too, so you
can see if it changes.

Hadley
